root_idea.summary: The root centers on hindering, preventing, or turning someone or something away from an intended course, especially a course of good.
root_idea.development: The core obstruction sense extends to agents who hinder, circumstances that impede achievement, states of being hindered, and several specialized or figurative usages. The evidence also records independent nominal usages involving hunger, sounds, a star, and an idol.

senses.definition: One who hinders, discourages, or turns people away from the good they seek; a hindering or obstructing agent.
senses.usage_conditions: The singular citation form is مُعَوِّق, the active participle of Form II عَوَّقَ; the Quranic occurrence is plural masculine and describes people who hold others back from advancing in the way of good.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the idiom مَا عَاقَتْ عِنْدَ زَوْجِهَا وَلَا لَاقَتْ: she did not cleave to her husband's heart; by another interpretation, she did not hinder him from separating from her or marrying another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression with variant reported interpretations, including that she was not happy with, favored by, or beloved by her husband.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To disable someone from carrying on a journey, as when a beast or travelling provisions fail; to put someone in difficulty so that the intended task cannot be completed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an impediment caused by failure of a means of travel or provision; the result is inability to accomplish the intended undertaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become hindered, held back, turned aside, or retarded by being occupied with something else.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive self-directed construction, also explained as becoming impeded from an affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be detained or retained with someone or at someone's abode; to be bound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported Classical usage distinct from the ordinary causative sense of hindering another person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The cry of a crow, or an imitation of that cry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An imitative expression; the orthographic variant عَاقِ عَاقِ is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where a valley bends or inclines to the right or left.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical or topographical noun, unrelated to the agentive obstruction sense except in form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Time or a period of time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression لَا يَكُونُ ذٰلِكَ آخِرَ عَوْقٍ, meaning that something will not continue until the end of time.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man in whom or with whom there is no good; a worthless or niggardly man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A personal epithet, including the reported poetic use for a niggardly person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hunger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal usage equated with عَوْلَقٌ in the cited lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hungry; very hungry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested adjectivally in the collocation رَجُلٌ عَوِقٌ لَوِقٌ; the example does not establish a restriction beyond the state of hunger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A coward or cowardly person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This sense is specifically reported as belonging to the dialect of Hudhayl.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One whom affairs continually hinder or prevent from accomplishing the object of his need.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a person repeatedly thwarted by circumstances rather than necessarily one who obstructs others.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who accomplishes a thing when he sets his mind on it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A contrary sense reported in the same lexical discussion and attributed to a named authority; it is retained separately from the obstruction senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sound issuing from the belly of a beast, horse, or similar animal while it is moving; by another report, a sound made by anything.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A sound term, with the animal-specific interpretation and a broader alternative both reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sound of a horse's penile sheath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical and zoological usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An accident or casualty of time or fortune that diverts, hinders, or occupies someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural عَوَائِقُ الدَّهْر denotes circumstances of time that impede a person by engrossing or employing them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Very niggardly or miserly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported in an imitative collocation; another report instead equates the word with the hinderer epithet عُوَقٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The bright star Capella, regarded in traditional description as impeding الدَّبَرَان from meeting the Pleiades.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed astronomical name; the evidence discusses alternative analyses of its medial consonant and its traditional stellar position.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One disappointed of attaining an object because a beast or travelling provisions have failed; one who has met with failure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for the resulting state of a person whose means of travel or provision have failed; equated with مُخْفِقٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hungry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported meaning of this headword, distinct from the sense of being disappointed by failed means.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of an idol associated with the people of Noah; other reports associate it with Kinānah or Murād.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper name in religious-historical usage, with variant accounts of the idol's original identity and tribal association.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The general hindering and turning-away branch is covered by the Quranic agent sense.
Distinct idiomatic usage concerning a wife and her husband's attachment or separation.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the preceding lexical sentence.
Pointer to the shared ordinary hindering sense.
Failure of a beast or provisions disabling a journey.
Being put in difficulty and unable to complete an undertaking.
Pointer to the ordinary hindering sense.
Distinct reported sense of being detained, retained, or bound.
The hinderer epithet is covered by the Quranic hindering-agent sense.
Topographical sense of a valley bend.
Contains the hinderer branch plus distinct cowardly, circumstantially thwarted, and contrary resolute senses.
Sound issuing from an animal's belly, with a broader alternative.
Contains the ordinary hindering-agent branch and the distinct accidents-of-time construction.
Imitative or independently interpreted sense of extreme niggardliness.
Contains distinct failure/disappointment and hunger meanings.
Idol name and its reported associations.

cautions: The عُوَقٌ entry reports both obstruction-related senses and a contrary sense of resolute accomplishment; these are retained as separately attributed Classical meanings.
The supplied packet contains no Maqāyīs entry, so the root-level orientation is based on the directly matched Quran-focused and Lane evidence.
